pr0.title: Replace msgpack with a minimal node ID encoder

nodes.body:
Hey @tj-smith47,

Thanks for putting this replacement together.

### Encoding compatibility

I wanted some runtime evidence that the replacement preserves the existing encoding, so I ran a standalone differential fuzz test against `github.com/vmihailenco/msgpack/v5` at `v5.4.1`. The harness uses the [helper at the reviewed commit](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/80256c3312f60dc13aee2b0a290df599705d3319/api/node_id.go#L1-L28) with the local API change shown below.

The test covers two- and three-element arrays with non-negative template indices and database IDs. It includes zero, used by the current callers, and nonzero template indices. The seeds exercise each integer-width boundary through `math.MaxInt64` in the template index and each database ID position.

<details>
<summary>Differential fuzz test source</summary>

```go
package api

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/base64"
	"math"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"github.com/vmihailenco/msgpack/v5"
)

// The implementation under test is copied from the local cli/cli#14801 changes
// that expose an explicit templateIndex parameter.
func FuzzEncodeNodeIDTemplateIndexMatchesMsgpack(f *testing.F) {
	for _, id := range []int64{
		0, 1,
		127, 128,
		math.MaxUint8, math.MaxUint8 + 1,
		math.MaxUint16, math.MaxUint16 + 1,
		math.MaxUint32, math.MaxUint32 + 1,
		math.MaxInt64,
	} {
		f.Add(int64(0), id, int64(0), false)
		f.Add(int64(0), id, int64(0), true)
		f.Add(int64(0), int64(0), id, true)
		f.Add(id, int64(0), int64(0), false)
		f.Add(id, int64(0), int64(0), true)
	}

	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, templateIndex, firstID, secondID int64, threeElements bool) {
		// Given a non-negative template index and database IDs
		if templateIndex < 0 || firstID < 0 || (threeElements && secondID < 0) {
			t.Skip("the encoder supports only non-negative template indices and database IDs")
		}
		ids := []int64{firstID}
		if threeElements {
			ids = append(ids, secondID)
		}
		var reference bytes.Buffer
		encoder := msgpack.NewEncoder(&reference)
		encoder.UseCompactInts(true)
		require.NoError(t, encoder.Encode(append([]int64{templateIndex}, ids...)))
		want := base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(reference.Bytes())

		// When the replacement encodes the same IDs
		got := EncodeNodeID(templateIndex, ids...)

		// Then its output matches the original dependency byte for byte
		assert.Equal(t, want, got, "template index: %d, IDs: %v", templateIndex, ids)
	})
}
```

</details>

The run passed with 3,477,554 fuzz executions and no mismatches.

<summary>Full differential fuzz run output</summary>

</details>

### Supported inputs

I made the leading value an explicit `templateIndex` parameter rather than hiding a zero inside `EncodeNodeID`. The existing callers still pass zero. I also made the helper's preconditions explicit. The updated helper used in the harness is:

<details>
<summary>Updated node ID encoder</summary>

```go
package api

import (
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
)

// EncodeNodeID encodes templateIndex and ids as a base64 MessagePack array
// of compact integers, the payload of a GraphQL node ID such as "PR_<payload>".
//
// templateIndex is an internal GitHub node ID detail. Clients should treat node
// IDs as opaque rather than construct them. This preserves existing behaviour
// for the dependency refactor. Removing this coupling is a separate change.
//
// templateIndex and all IDs must be non-negative. Callers must supply fewer
// than 15 IDs.
func EncodeNodeID(templateIndex int64, ids ...int64) string {
	parts := append([]int64{templateIndex}, ids...)
	b := []byte{0x90 | byte(len(parts))}
	for _, id := range parts {
		switch {
		case id < 0x80:
			b = append(b, byte(id))
		case id <= math.MaxUint8:
			b = append(b, 0xcc, byte(id))
		case id <= math.MaxUint16:
			b = binary.BigEndian.AppendUint16(append(b, 0xcd), uint16(id))
		case id <= math.MaxUint32:
			b = binary.BigEndian.AppendUint32(append(b, 0xce), uint32(id))
		default:
			b = binary.BigEndian.AppendUint64(append(b, 0xcf), uint64(id))
		}
	}
	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(b)
}
```

</details>

The fuzz test covers non-negative template indices and IDs in the two payload shapes used by the current callers, not general MessagePack equivalence.

`templateIndex` is an internal GitHub node ID detail, and [clients should treat node IDs as opaque](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/guides/migrating-graphql-global-node-ids#determining-if-you-need-to-take-action). I don't think `gh` should need to construct these IDs, but that coupling already exists. This pure refactor away from `msgpack/v5` preserves the existing behaviour, rather than trying to remove that coupling in the same change.

### Live acceptance tests

Both discussion acceptance scripts passed at [034580f](https://github.com/cli/cli/commit/034580fb43f7219b501a6ac83b878f3a44df1fcc), covering `gh discussion` reply, edit, delete, and view behaviour using comment URLs.

```text
$ bash /Users/williammartin/.copilot/skills/run-acceptance-tests/scripts/run.sh --repo-root /Users/williammartin/workspace/work/copilot-worktrees/cli/williammartin-redesigned-chainsaw --approved-head-sha 034580fb43f7219b501a6ac83b878f3a44df1fcc discussion/discussion-comment.txtar discussion/discussion-view.txtar
Running discussion acceptance scripts from the current working tree: discussion-comment.txtar,discussion-view.txtar
ok  	github.com/cli/cli/v2/acceptance	38.708s
```

### 🟢 Approval recommended The narrow replacement preserves encoding for supported inputs, has boundary and caller-level test coverage, and has no unresolved findings. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR Replaces msgpack with a small shared encoder for GitHub GraphQL node IDs, addressing #14800 while preserving encoding for the documented non-negative inputs. **Changes:** - Adds a compact-integer encoder with integer-width boundary tests. - Migrates pull request, user, and discussion comment node ID generation to the shared helper. - Removes msgpack and its tagparser dependency. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `pkg/​cmd/​discussion/​client/​client.go` | Uses the shared encoder for discussion comment IDs. | | `pkg/​cmd/​agent-task/​capi/​sessions.go` | Uses the shared encoder for pull request and user IDs. | | `go.sum` | Removes msgpack and tagparser checksums. | | `go.mod` | Removes msgpack and tagparser dependencies. | | `api/​node_id.go` | Adds the minimal node ID payload encoder. | | `api/​node_id_test.go` | Tests integer-width boundaries and a nonzero template index. |
Review effort: Balanced

pr1.title: release download: add --verify to check immutability and build provenance before downloading

nodes.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Contribution eligibility, existing stdout compatibility, and verification-policy test coverage remain unresolved.
3 open issues - [Preserve stdout behavior for downloads named -](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14783#discussion_r4339733038) · New - [Test Sigstore policy enforcement and signer constraints](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14783#discussion_r4339733147) · New - [Establish contribution eligibility before implementation](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14783#discussion_r4339733201) · New
What changed in this PR Adds optional pre-download attestation checks to `gh release download`, reusing the existing verification infrastructure. **Changes:** - Adds `--verify` and release asset URL input. - Reports release immutability and build provenance before confirmation. - Stages downloads and checks digests before publishing files or stdout. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | pkg/​cmd/​release/​download/​provenance.go | Implements attestation checks, reporting, and confirmation. | | pkg/​cmd/​release/​download/​provenance_test.go | Tests verification flows, URL parsing, and staged downloads. | | pkg/​cmd/​release/​download/​download.go | Wires verification, staging, digest checks, and output routing. | | pkg/​cmd/​release/​download/​download_test.go | Updates the download helper invocation. |
Review effort: Balanced

Two design questions here can be answered with data, so I measured before commenting.

**How common is each state today?** Sample: latest release of 15 well-known single-binary CLI projects, linux/amd64 archive, queried 2026-10-27 via `gh api` (`releases/latest` + `GET /repos/{r}/attestations/{digest}`):

- immutable release: **3/15** (`cli/cli`, `astral-sh/uv`, `mikefarah/yq`)
- attestation present for the advertised asset digest: **6/15** (`cli/cli`, `jqlang/jq`, `sharkdp/fd`, `astral-sh/uv`, `atuinsh/atuin`, `mikefarah/yq`); the other 9 return 404 (`ripgrep`, `bat`, `delta`, `neovim`, `helix`, `fzf`, `zellij`, `task`, `k9s`)
- `.digest` populated on the asset object: **15/15** — so "does provenance exist for this asset?" can be answered *before* downloading, without trusting any bytes yet.

**Mutable release with valid provenance — pass silently in scripts?** I think yes, with a warning, because provenance and immutability prove different things. Checked end to end on a mutable release (`sharkdp/fd` v10.5.0, `immutable=false`): `gh attestation verify` binds the file to `sha256 a1259cd…`, `sourceRepositoryURI https://github.com/sharkdp/fd`, workflow `CICD.yml@refs/tags/v10.5.0`, source commit `4f81778…`. That already rules out a swapped asset. What it does *not* rule out is the release page being repointed later (to an older or differently-built but attested artifact of the same repo), which is exactly what immutability/the release attestation covers. So: provenance pass + mutable release → warn and continue; make hard failure opt-in (`--verify=required` or a separate `--require-immutable`). Failing on mutable by default would reject 12/15 of the sample above, and those users would learn to pass the "skip" flag by reflex.

Because of that split, `--verify` looks like two phases: a pre-download check (release attestation / `immutable`, and whether an attestation exists for the asset digest) plus the actual cryptographic check *after* the bytes are on disk. Streaming to stdout (`--output -`) can't be verified before use — worth stating in the help text rather than silently passing.

Two smaller points: a `*checksums.txt` from the same release is not a trust anchor (same publisher, same mutable surface), so it shouldn't be displayed as a verified signal; and "no attestation found via the API" should be worded distinctly from "attestation failed" — `jqlang/jq` ships its bundle *inside* the release (`jq-attestation.json`) instead of the attestation store, so a user there gets a 404 today and would read it as tampering.

Happy to test a build against that 15-repo list if you want a compatibility pass.

🛑 Requirement: Preserve stdout behavior without --verify

Downloading an asset named `-` into the current directory now creates a file instead of streaming its bytes to stdout, even without `--verify`. Existing pipelines receive no data, and an existing file can make a previously successful invocation fail. The description documents this break but supplies no maintainer approval, as required by docs/command-development.md:66-69. Preserve the legacy route for ordinary downloads and keep staging file-only, or obtain explicit approval for the compatibility change. Update the regression test to reflect the agreed behavior.

🛑 Requirement: Test the policy passed to Sigstore

All new download verification tests use a stub that ignores the policy argument (provenance_test.go:178-179). They therefore cannot detect removal or misconfiguration of the attested-digest binding or signer certificate identity constraint; the tampered-download cases test only the later byte hash. Add offline policy-level tests showing that mismatched attested digests and signer identities are rejected, and that an allowed reusable-workflow signer is accepted. Use isolated fixtures or policy inspection to exercise this command's assembled policy, consistent with docs/testing.md:49-50.

🛑 Requirement: Establish contribution eligibility

The description says there is no tracking issue, and the supplied context does not establish maintainer authorization. .github/CONTRIBUTING.md:5 requires external contributions to target an issue labelled help wanted with explicit acceptance criteria. Please obtain clarification from `@cli/code-reviewers` through an issue/discussion, or establish trusted maintainer authorization for this scope before continuing the upstream implementation. Draft status does not satisfy this prerequisite.
